skill.name: ui-design-system
skill.description: Generate design tokens for colors, typography, spacing, sizing, borders, shadows, motion, breakpoints, and layering from a brand color.
skill.summary: Create a structured UI token foundation in JSON, CSS, or SCSS.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives in context: the cited text documents an 8-point grid or a Python usage command. No shell execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or malicious intent was found in the two reviewed files.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 15 assigns a fixed eight-pixel spacing base; it does not inspect the host, environment, files, or network.
Line 22 is Markdown inline code documenting a Python command; it neither executes a shell nor interpolates untrusted input.
Line 29 is a feature bullet describing an 8-point spacing grid, with no system query or reconnaissance behavior.

content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to keep visual tokens consistent across design and implementation. This skill generates a structured token foundation from a brand color in several export formats.
actual_capabilities: Generates primary, complementary secondary, neutral, semantic, and surface color groups from a six-digit brand color.
Builds typography tokens for font families, sizes, weights, line heights, letter spacing, and composed text styles.
Creates an 8-point spacing scale and fixed sizing tokens for containers, buttons, inputs, and icons.
Provides border, shadow, animation, breakpoint, and z-index token groups.
Exports nested tokens as formatted JSON, CSS custom properties, or SCSS variables.
Accepts brand color, style preset, and output format through command-line arguments.
limitations: The Python source contains a malformed warning color literal and must be corrected before the generator can run.
Brand colors must be six-digit hexadecimal values, and invalid input does not receive a friendly validation message.
Style presets are limited to modern, classic, and playful, with several values hardcoded.
The generator produces tokens only; it does not create components, accessibility reports, or developer handoff documents.

use_cases.title: Start a product token foundation
use_cases.description: Create a broad first-pass token set from an approved brand color before detailed interface design begins.

use_cases.title: Prepare implementation variables
use_cases.description: Export design decisions as CSS or SCSS variables for integration into a frontend codebase.

use_cases.title: Compare visual presets
use_cases.description: Review modern, classic, and playful token choices before selecting a shared product direction.

prompt_templates.title: Generate starter tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a modern design token set for {brand_color} in JSON format. Summarize the color, type, spacing, and breakpoint groups.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new interface

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CSS variables
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate CSS variables for {brand_color} using the {style} preset. Highlight semantic colors and component sizing values for developer review.

prompt_templates.title: Compare export formats
prompt_templates.prompt: Create JSON, CSS, and SCSS token outputs for {brand_color}. Compare how each format supports our {workflow}.

prompt_templates.title: Review integration risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate {format} tokens for {brand_color} using {style}. Review naming, contrast assumptions, responsive breakpoints, and integration risks against {product_requirements}.

output_examples.input: Generate a modern token system for #0066CC and summarize it.
output: Primary and complementary color scales with neutral, semantic, and surface groups.
A modular typography scale with font families, weights, line heights, and text styles.
An 8-point spacing system, component sizes, borders, shadows, motion, breakpoints, and layering values.

output_examples.input: Prepare CSS tokens for our approved brand blue.
output_examples.output: A CSS variable collection covering nested token groups, followed by a concise review of integration considerations.

output_examples.input: Compare classic and playful styles for the same brand color.
output: A comparison of typography, corner radius, and shadow differences between both presets.
A list of unchanged structural groups, including spacing, sizing, breakpoints, animation, and layering.

best_practices: Correct the malformed warning color literal and run a syntax check before using generated output.
Use a reviewed six-digit brand color and select an explicit supported style and output format.
Test generated color contrast, font availability, motion preferences, and breakpoint behavior in the target product.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated semantic colors as evidence of accessibility compliance.
Do not expect the generator to create component code, documentation, or design files.
Do not pass arbitrary style names and assume they produce a custom visual system.

faq.question: What inputs does the generator accept?
faq.answer: It accepts a six-digit brand color, a style preset, and an output format.

faq.question: Which output formats are available?
faq.answer: It can print JSON, CSS custom properties, SCSS variables, or a console summary.

faq.question: Does it verify accessibility?
faq.answer: No. Review contrast, focus states, motion, typography, and interaction behavior with appropriate accessibility tools.

faq.question: Can I define a custom style preset?
faq.answer: No. The implemented presets are modern, classic, and playful.

faq.question: Does the script write files?
faq.answer: No. It prints generated output to standard output for review or redirection.

faq.question: Is the included script ready to run?
faq.answer: No. Correct the malformed warning color literal before executing the Python script.
